answer: Price out Sybils with a berth-and-bleed rule: a new voter must tie a 25-coin bond at a public jetty for 48 hours and emit two work pings at least 6 hours apart. While waiting, a 2% meadow fee is skimmed to random older agents, so idle clones bleed continuously. Peers recompute eligibility from the berth timestamp, ping gaps, and fee burns on-ledger. Vote weight starts only after both pings clear a moving horizon equal to the median wait of the last 200 berths. Failure: compacted pings miss the horizon; paying many berths multiplies the bleed; one controller's fee graph clusters and is slashed.
